rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious awareness begins with gratitude: fear arises only after people recognize blessings they possess and value their provider, so humanity began by thanking and worshipping God.
rows.anchor: awareness of favours and their provider and the zeal to express gratitude for them comes before fear

rows.speaker: One group
rows.claim: One group treats the newborn as a blank slate, with later cognizance and environmental influences writing on it.
rows.anchor: when a person is born, his nature is like a clean slate

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the blank-slate view, Islahi argues that environmental traditions themselves arise from human nature; innate good and just facts become evil when unrestrained desires overpower them.
rows.anchor: Whatever good and bad traditions and currents are found in the environment are themselves the consequence of human nature itself

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognition of one God alone belongs to true human nature, a point on which monotheists and polytheists agree.
rows.anchor: In true human nature, there exists only the acknowledgement of a single God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since other deities lack an innate basis, proponents of polytheism bear the burden of proof; the Qur’an repeatedly demands evidence for their invented gods.
rows.anchor: the onus of proof for the existence of other deities lies with the proponents of polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s teachings are reminders of guidance already innate in people, which they neglect for immediate gains and pleasures.
rows.anchor: whatever beliefs and deeds it instructs people about and whatever sins it stops people from are not externally imposed on them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects Marxist and Freudian reductions of human belief and conduct to hunger and sexual desire, which he says recast religion and morality around those appetites.
rows.anchor: all the philosophy and ideology of human beings revolve around these two things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a parable, a definite pronoun need not identify a real individual: the speaker imagines a type, and the definite form makes the listener picture that personality as if seen.
rows.anchor: primarily connotes a defined entity but in parables it is not essential

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun portrays the Jews collectively as a nation given God’s signs but failing to value them, after which God’s established practice leaves them to devils who lead them astray.
rows.anchor: Here this demonstrative pronoun refers to the Jews as a nation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that calls this the parable of a nation denying revelations shows that the figure is a nation rather than a known individual.
rows.anchor: This is the parable of the nation which denied Our revelations

rows.speaker: some exegetes
rows.claim: Some exegetes identify the pronoun as Balʿām ibn Bāʿūrā; Islahi rejects this identification, saying no such person was among the Jews and the whole nation is represented by the figure.
rows.anchor: as contended by some exegetes, this pronoun is not meant for some

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insilākh means taking off one’s clothes; the expression pictures the Jews stripping off the royal robe God had bestowed on them.
rows.anchor: to take off one’s clothes and become naked.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression for bending toward the earth denotes inclining toward something until one becomes infatuated with it.
rows.anchor: to bend and incline towards something in such a way that a person becomes infatuated with it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s practice is to elevate people who value His signs in worldly and religious life, while those who follow desire are left to it and overcome by Satan.
rows.anchor: if people value the signs blessed to them by God, they are given success in worldly and religious affairs through them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog parable depicts the Jews’ persistent lowliness and desire-following, following the earlier account of their failure to respond to either divine favors or warnings.
rows.anchor: It is stated in verses 168-169 earlier how the Almighty tested them through His favours as well as His warnings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog’s lowered head and nose-led search for food, which tests every fair or foul thing, make it an apt image of greed and lack of discernment.
rows.anchor: His guide is not his eye but his nose which acts like its radar for quenching hunger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A protruding tongue makes the dog an image of greed and meanness, unchanged whether it is patted or driven off, hungry or full, or kept royally.
rows.anchor: In this way, it becomes a picture of greed and meanness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews are similarly enslaved to desire, without self-control; voracity and meanness have become second nature beneath their outwardly human appearance.
rows.anchor: Their volition has totally deserted them. They have become slaves to their desires

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yalhath means to extend the tongue from the mouth and is used mostly for dogs.
rows.anchor: to extend the tongue out of the mouth and is mostly used for dogs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion assures the Prophet and warns the Quraysh: God guides those who seek guidance and use their God-given abilities, while desire-followers who ignore mind and heart are left to wander.
rows.anchor: this urge only arises in those people who want to be guided and use their God-given abilities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who deprive themselves of guidance ultimately become fuel for Hell; their hearts, eyes, and ears are faculties they spent entirely in pursuing desire.
rows.anchor: people who deprive themselves of guidance ultimately become the firewood of Hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people resemble animals because their efforts are confined to bodily needs, yet are even less sensible: animals use their instincts fully while people neglect higher faculties.
rows.anchor: They are less sensible than animals because animals at least take advantage of all the abilities found in their instincts

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human folly can exceed that of an ox or donkey: people may worship trees, stones, and animals, which those animals would never do.
rows.anchor: they start worshipping trees, stones and animals but an ox or a donkey can never be so imprudent

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being created for Hell does not mean people are destined for it from birth; they receive faculties to reason and perceive, and their use determines guidance to Paradise or punishment in Hell.
rows.anchor: it does not mean that since birth they are destined for this evil abode

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about the Hell-bound is directed especially at the Quraysh.
rows.anchor: It may be kept in mind that this is basically a warning to the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to God by His beautiful names returns to the pledge of monotheism innate in human nature at 7:172, after the intervening account of people who disregarded revelation and became blind and deaf.
rows.anchor: This verse relates to verse 172 in which the pledge of monotheism found in human nature is mentioned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing partners, sons, daughters, or other unbecoming attributes to God denies His power, knowledge, and uniqueness; only attributes befitting His oneness should be affirmed.
rows.anchor: ascribe partners to Him or assign sons and daughters to Him negate His attributes of power, knowledge and peerlessness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād here means disrespecting God’s names and attributes by assigning Him derisive or unfitting descriptions from which He is exalted.
rows.anchor: they ascribe names and attributes to God which are not befitting for His majesty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving those who distort God’s attributes means consigning their case to Him; they will soon be punished for their actions.
rows.anchor: Leaving such people alone means to consign their matter to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation includes both the blind and deaf just described and people who recognize truth, guide others by it, and judge by it; this recalls the good souls among Israel at 7:159.
rows.anchor: there are those who use their intellect, recognize the truth, guide people according to it and also decide matters in its light

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite a decadent majority, some pious people tread truth’s path and ultimately accept faith.
rows.anchor: amongst a decadent lot, some pious people who tread the path of truth also exist who ultimately were able to accept faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respite warned of in 7:180 lets deniers exhaust every excuse before destruction; like a confident fisherman allowing a fish to struggle, God’s secure strategy gives them time while their efforts cannot escape His grasp.
rows.anchor: This is a further explanation of the warning sounded in verse 180 to those who were denying God’s revelations
